cells.tense: You're here, doing the work, and you don't need to see where it ends.
cells.verb: taking the next step by the little light you have
cells.place: in the hours you spend alone getting good at something by doing it again
cells.ask: Let the practice want something. Point it at one place you'd actually like to arrive, not because you can see the whole way there but because the wanting is real — and let the picture of where you're going keep coming from what your hands have already learned.
cells.core: You're here, doing the work, and you don't need to see where it ends. Each session gives you enough to do the next one, and that's been enough — you're not forcing the road to show itself before you'll walk it. What you picture when you practice isn't a fantasy laid over the work; it grew out of the work. The doing and the dreaming are the same motion.
cells.sheetLine: You practice by the light you have, and the dream comes from the doing.

cells.tense: You're already living in the version where this is finished and you're someone else.
cells.verb: filling the not-knowing with a picture instead of a step
cells.place: in the hours you spend alone getting good at something by doing it again
cells.ask: Tend the one thing that's actually growing. Give today's small rep exactly what it needs and let it be as small as it is, without asking it to be the whole future — and watch what you picture start coming from what you've done instead of from what you've promised yourself.
cells.core: You're already living in the version where this is finished and you're someone else. Every session carries so much meaning that the session itself gets thin — the imagined mastery is standing where the work should be, and the gap between them is the thing you keep bracing against. The dream was supposed to light the next step. It's started replacing it.
cells.sheetLine: The picture of who you'll be has started standing in for the work.

cells.tense: Somewhere behind you, following a hunch cost something, and you're still paying it off.
cells.verb: refusing the step you can't fully see
cells.place: in the hours you spend alone getting good at something by doing it again
cells.ask: Don't force the dreaming back. Instead, notice what you already know matters before you can explain why — then follow one of those noticings in your next session and see if it proves right. The knowing fills first; the picturing comes back behind it, grown from everything the repetition has taught you.
cells.core: Somewhere behind you, following a hunch cost something, and you're still paying it off. Now only what can be counted gets to count — the exact form, the measured rep, nothing that can't be checked. The practice is still happening. It's just not allowed to mean anything beyond itself, and a practice that can't dream stops showing you where it's going.
cells.sheetLine: You drill the form and have stopped trusting the hunch.

cells.tense: You're already being steered by a picture, and you'd tell anyone you're just doing the work.
cells.verb: moving through the not-knowing without noticing you're being led
cells.place: in the hours you spend alone getting good at something by doing it again
cells.ask: Strip one session back to a single plain rep done for its own sake, no goal attached — and watch what you reach for anyway. Whatever you keep reaching for is the dream that's been running you. Say what it is, once, and let the practice start dreaming on purpose from what it has already learned.
cells.core: You're already being steered by a picture, and you'd tell anyone you're just doing the work. But look at which exercises you choose, which you skip, what you linger on — something is choosing, and it isn't the drill. There's a vision shaping every solitary hour and the one person it belongs to hasn't looked at it.
cells.sheetLine: A dream is picking your reps. You call it routine.
